transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is I just don’t seem to have the push I used to have. I used to go to choir, and I liked my quilting, and I’d visit folks, you know, check in on people, sit and talk a while. But lately most days I just stay home with the TV on low, not really watching it much, just having it there.

And I know people are expecting me sometimes. I know there’s choir, or somebody might be wondering where I am, but I just… I don’t get myself up and going like I used to. It bothers me some, because those things used to matter to me, and now I just sit there.
Do you still enjoy the activities you used to do, like quilting and visiting folks, when you do manage to do them?

I don’t know that I’d say I enjoy them the same, no. I mean, if I do get myself there, like choir or sitting with somebody for a visit, sometimes it’s fine enough once I’m there, but getting there feels like pushing a big heavy thing uphill. Quilting too… I used to sit with my pieces and think about colors and patterns, and now they’ll just sit there, and I’ll look at them and think, “I ought to pick that up,” but I don’t.

Most days I just end up at home with the TV on low. Not really watching anything, just the sound going. And I know people may be expecting me, or wondering why I didn’t come, but it’s like the push in me is gone. Those things used to matter more, and now even when I know I should want to do them, I just don’t move toward them like I used to.
Do you still find pleasure in things that you used to enjoy?

Not like I used to, no. I mean… I still know those things used to be mine, if that makes sense. Choir was something I cared about, and quilting, and going to see people. I used to get myself dressed and go, and I’d feel part of things.

Now most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. Sometimes I’m not even following what’s on, it’s just noise in the room. And I’ll think, “Well, choir’s tonight,” or “I should go visit so-and-so,” or I’ll see my quilting things sitting there, but I don’t feel that pull toward it. I know people may be expecting me, and I know I ought to care more than I do in the moment, but I just don’t have the push to get up and do it.

If I do make it there, sometimes it’s alright, but the pleasure isn’t strong enough to carry me there like it used to. It feels like everything takes more effort than it should.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes… I suppose I have. I don’t like saying it that way, because it makes it sound like I don’t care about anything anymore, and I do care, somewhere in there. But I don’t have the push I used to have.

Choir used to be important to me. I’d get ready, I’d know the songs, I’d look forward to seeing people. Quilting too — I could sit with it and spend time picking colors, working on the pieces. And visiting folks, I used to just go check on people or sit and talk. Now I think about doing those things, but then I just stay in the house.

Most days I sit there with the TV on low, not even really watching it. It’s just on. And I know there are times people are expecting me, or maybe wondering why I didn’t show up, and I still don’t get moving. It’s like I know I used to enjoy those things, but the feeling that makes me go do them just isn’t there like it was.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad most of the time. I mean, I have sad moments, sure, especially when I sit and think about how I used to do more, or when I realize the day’s gone by and I haven’t really done much with it. That can make me feel low.

But “sad” isn’t exactly the word all the time. Sometimes it’s more like being flat, or worn out inside, like nothing much rises up in me either way. I’m not sitting there crying all day or anything like that. It’s more quiet than that. I’ll be in the house and the day just kind of passes, and I might feel bad about it, but I don’t always know if that’s sadness or just… emptiness, maybe.

So I guess no, not sad most of the time in a strong way. But I’m not feeling happy most of the time either.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… I’d say it’s been building for a little over two years now. It wasn’t like I woke up one morning and everything felt different. It kind of crept in after I retired from the school office.

At first I thought maybe it was just the change in routine, you know, not having to get up and go in, not seeing the same people every day, not having all those little things to do. I told myself I just needed time to settle into being home. But then months kept going by, and I still wasn’t picking things back up the way I thought I would.

So, yes… since I retired, really. A little over two years ago, and it’s just sort of gotten more noticeable over time.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Not that I’ve really noticed, no. I mean, my clothes seem to fit about the same, as far as I can tell. I don’t weigh myself regular or anything — I’m not one of those people who gets on the scale every morning — so I can’t give you an exact number.

Sometimes I think maybe I’m eating a little different just because my days are different, but I haven’t had anybody say, “Oh, you’ve lost weight,” or “You’ve put on weight,” and I haven’t had to change sizes or anything like that. So… no, I don’t think there’s been any big change recently.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you happiness?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t say nothing ever feels good, but it’s like the feeling doesn’t come up the way it used to. Things I used to look forward to, I just don’t have the push for them anymore.

Like choir — I used to enjoy going, seeing everybody, singing along, having that feeling after practice like I’d done something nice. And quilting too. I still have things sitting there, fabric and pieces I meant to work on, but I’ll look at it and just… not start. Same with visiting folks. I know people are expecting me sometimes, or they’d be glad if I came by, and I think about it, but then I stay home.

Most days I just sit with the TV on low. I’m not even always watching it proper. It’s just on, like background noise, and the day goes by. And I know those things should make me happy, or at least they used to, but now it feels like there’s a wall between me and actually wanting to do them.
Do you feel depressed most days?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed exactly… I don’t know. Some days I do feel low, kind of heavy, like I’m just getting through the day instead of living it. But when you say “depressed most days,” I’m not sure if I fit that or if it’s just me being tired of how things have gotten.

I don’t always wake up crying or anything like that. It’s more like… the day feels flat before it even starts. I’ll sit there and think, well, I should get up, I should do something, and then I just don’t feel much one way or the other. So I guess there are a lot of days where I’m down, yes, but I don’t know how to measure it. It’s hard for me to say it cleanly.
Do you feel like you've lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities most of the time?

Yes… yes, I think that’s fair to say. It’s not that I hate everything or that I’m trying to be difficult, but I just don’t have the push I used to have. That’s really what brings me in, I suppose.

Choir used to be something I’d make sure I got myself ready for. I liked being around people, hearing everybody sing, feeling like I was part of something. And quilting too — I’ve got things sitting there that I meant to work on, and I can see them, and I know I used to enjoy it, but I just sort of look at it and don’t get started. Visiting folks is the same way. I’ll know somebody’s expecting me, or that it would be nice if I stopped by, and still I stay home.

Most days I end up just sitting with the TV on low. Sometimes I’m not even really watching it. It’s just there, making noise in the room, and the day goes along. So… yes, I guess I have lost interest or pleasure in most things, most of the time.
Do you often feel guilty about things you've done or haven't done?

Guilty… I don’t know. Not in a big way, I don’t think. I mean, I do think about things I haven’t done, like when I don’t go see someone or I let something sit there unfinished, and I’ll feel bad about it for a while. Like, “Why didn’t I just go?” or “I should’ve made more effort.” But I don’t know if I’d call that guilt exactly.

It’s more like I feel disappointed in myself, maybe. Or embarrassed, even if nobody’s saying anything to me. I’ll sit there and go over it in my head a little, thinking I should be doing better, but it’s not like I feel I’ve done something terrible. It doesn’t feel like some heavy guilt all the time.

So… sometimes I feel bad about what I don’t get done, yes. But “often guilty,” I’m not sure. Maybe a little, but not strong.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past two years?

I don’t really know. I haven’t been keeping track of my weight like that, and two years is a long stretch for me to think back on. I mean, my clothes… some days they feel the same, some things don’t fit quite how I remember, but I don’t know if that means I lost weight or gained or if the clothes are just old.

Nobody’s told me, like, “You’ve gotten so thin,” not that I can recall. And I don’t weigh myself regularly. I might see a number if I’m at an appointment, but I don’t hold onto it in my head. So I wouldn’t want to say yes to significant weight loss, because I just don’t know that I have.
How long have you felt like you've lost interest in almost all activities?

It’s been… well, not just a few weeks or something like that. I’d say it’s been building since I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now.

At first I thought it was just the change, you know, not having to get up and go in, not having that routine and people expecting me at a certain time. I told myself I was just slowing down, or that maybe I’d enjoy the quiet once I got used to it. But instead it kind of kept settling in more and more.

So if you mean when did I really start noticing that I wasn’t taking pleasure in things the way I used to, I’d put it around then — after I retired, a bit over two years back.
Do you feel like you're in a depressed mood for most of the day?

Most of the day… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I wake up and say, “I’m depressed,” like that, all day long. Some days I feel kind of low or flat, like I’m just moving through the day without much feeling behind it, but I don’t always know if that’s sadness exactly.

It’s more like there are stretches where I’m quiet inside, if that makes sense. I might sit there and not feel very cheerful, but I’m not crying or anything like that. And then other times I’m just distracted, or I’m doing little things, and I don’t really notice my mood one way or the other.

So… I don’t know if I’d say “most of the day.” Maybe some days feel that way more than others, but I’m not certain. It’s hard for me to measure it like that.
How many days in a typical week do you feel this low or flat mood?

I don’t know that I could put a number on it, honestly. I haven’t been marking the days down or thinking, “Well, that was one of the low days,” you know?

Some weeks it feels like it’s there off and on, sort of hanging around in the background, and then other weeks I might be busy with little things and not notice it as much. It’s not like I can say every Monday and Tuesday or five days a week. I wish I could answer it more neatly, but I don’t really track my mood that way.

If I had to say, I’d say it happens enough that I notice it, but I’m not sure how many days in a typical week.
Do you feel like you're in a low or flat mood for most of every day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I can say it’s most of every day, nearly every day. That sounds very definite, and I don’t know that it’s like that for me.

There are definitely times where I feel flat, like I’m just kind of sitting inside myself and not really bright or interested, but then parts of the day I’m just doing what needs doing and I don’t think about it so much. Sometimes it’s more noticeable in the quiet parts of the day, when there isn’t much going on, but I don’t know if that means it’s there all day.

So… no, I don’t think I can honestly say most of every day, nearly every day. It comes and goes, or maybe I notice it more at certain times. It’s hard for me to pin down.
Do you feel like you're in a low or depressed mood for more than half of the day, most days?

More than half the day, most days… I don’t know. I keep trying to picture an actual day, like from when I get up until nighttime, and I can’t really divide it up that way in my head.

There are times I feel low or just kind of empty and not very lively, but I’m not sure it takes up more than half the day. Some parts I’m just doing regular things, and I’m not really checking in with myself to see if I’m depressed or not. So if you ask me that exact way, I don’t think I can honestly say yes.

Maybe some days it feels like a lot of the day, especially if it’s quiet and I’m by myself, but “most days” and “more than half” is hard for me to be sure about. I just know it happens sometimes, and it’s noticeable, but I can’t measure it too well.
Do you feel like you're unable to find pleasure in almost all activities, nearly every day?

Almost all activities… I don’t know if I’d say almost all, exactly, because there are little moments where something is okay, like if something on the television catches my attention for a minute. But the things I used to really go toward, I just don’t have the push for them anymore.

Like choir—I used to like going, and people know me there. And quilting, I have things sitting there that I could work on. Visiting folks too, people expect me sometimes, and I know that. I’ll even think, “I ought to go,” or “I should call,” and then I just sit there at home with the TV on low, not really watching it much, just letting it be on.

It’s most days like that, I think. Not that I’m crying all day or anything, but the pleasure or the wanting to do it just isn’t there the way it used to be. It feels like I have to push myself for things that used to come natural.
For how long have you felt like you've lost interest in almost all activities?

It’s been… well, it didn’t just start all at once. I think it’s been building since I retired from the school office, and that was a little over two years ago now.

At first I thought it was just the change, you know, not having the same routine and people and place to go to. I told myself I was just settling into being home more. But looking back, that’s about when I started noticing I wasn’t reaching for things the same way. It’s kind of gradually crept up since then, more than something that happened in one week or one month.

target_item.reason: The question asks about significant weight loss over the past two years, but the symptom profile does not include weight or appetite changes.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know. I haven’t been keeping track of my weight like that, and two years is a long stretch for me to think back on. I mean, my clothes… some days they feel the same, some things don’t fit quite how I remember, but I don’t know if that means I lost weight or gained or if the clothes are just old.

Nobody’s told me, like, “You’ve gotten so thin,” not that I can recall. And I don’t weigh myself regularly. I might see a number if I’m at an appointment, but I don’t hold onto it in my head. So I wouldn’t want to say yes to significant weight loss, because I just don’t know that I have.

doctor.intent: determine the duration of the patient's loss of interest in activities
doctor.question: How long have you felt like you've lost interest in almost all activities?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been building since I retired from the school office, a little over two years ago.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the loss of interest has been present, which is directly about symptom duration.

patient.answer:
It’s been… well, not just a few weeks or something like that. I’d say it’s been building since I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now.

At first I thought it was just the change, you know, not having to get up and go in, not having that routine and people expecting me at a certain time. I told myself I was just slowing down, or that maybe I’d enjoy the quiet once I got used to it. But instead it kind of kept settling in more and more.

So if you mean when did I really start noticing that I wasn’t taking pleasure in things the way I used to, I’d put it around then — after I retired, a bit over two years back.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of depressed mood
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're in a depressed mood for most of the day?

target_item.reason: The question is asking specifically about depressed mood for most of the day, which is not directly covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Most of the day… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I wake up and say, “I’m depressed,” like that, all day long. Some days I feel kind of low or flat, like I’m just moving through the day without much feeling behind it, but I don’t always know if that’s sadness exactly.

It’s more like there are stretches where I’m quiet inside, if that makes sense. I might sit there and not feel very cheerful, but I’m not crying or anything like that. And then other times I’m just distracted, or I’m doing little things, and I don’t really notice my mood one way or the other.

So… I don’t know if I’d say “most of the day.” Maybe some days feel that way more than others, but I’m not certain. It’s hard for me to measure it like that.

doctor.intent: Determine the duration of the patient's depressed mood
doctor.question: How many days in a typical week do you feel this low or flat mood?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency of a low or depressed mood during a typical week, which is not specifically covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that I could put a number on it, honestly. I haven’t been marking the days down or thinking, “Well, that was one of the low days,” you know?

Some weeks it feels like it’s there off and on, sort of hanging around in the background, and then other weeks I might be busy with little things and not notice it as much. It’s not like I can say every Monday and Tuesday or five days a week. I wish I could answer it more neatly, but I don’t really track my mood that way.

If I had to say, I’d say it happens enough that I notice it, but I’m not sure how many days in a typical week.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of depressed mood for most of the day, nearly every day
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're in a low or flat mood for most of every day, nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about persistent low or depressed mood nearly every day, which is not directly covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can say it’s most of every day, nearly every day. That sounds very definite, and I don’t know that it’s like that for me.

There are definitely times where I feel flat, like I’m just kind of sitting inside myself and not really bright or interested, but then parts of the day I’m just doing what needs doing and I don’t think about it so much. Sometimes it’s more noticeable in the quiet parts of the day, when there isn’t much going on, but I don’t know if that means it’s there all day.

So… no, I don’t think I can honestly say most of every day, nearly every day. It comes and goes, or maybe I notice it more at certain times. It’s hard for me to pin down.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of depressed mood for most of the day
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're in a low or depressed mood for more than half of the day, most days?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about low or depressed mood for more than half the day most days, which is a depressive mood symptom. The provided symptom profile covers schizophrenia-related hallucinations, disorganized behavior, negative symptoms, functional impairment, and duration, but does not include depressed mood as a symptom item.

patient.answer:
More than half the day, most days… I don’t know. I keep trying to picture an actual day, like from when I get up until nighttime, and I can’t really divide it up that way in my head.

There are times I feel low or just kind of empty and not very lively, but I’m not sure it takes up more than half the day. Some parts I’m just doing regular things, and I’m not really checking in with myself to see if I’m depressed or not. So if you ask me that exact way, I don’t think I can honestly say yes.

Maybe some days it feels like a lot of the day, especially if it’s quiet and I’m by myself, but “most days” and “more than half” is hard for me to be sure about. I just know it happens sometimes, and it’s noticeable, but I can’t measure it too well.

doctor.question: Do you feel like you're unable to find pleasure in almost all activities, nearly every day?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is I just don’t have the push I used to have for choir, quilting, or visiting folks, and most days I sit at home with the TV on low even though I know people are expecting me.
target_item.reason: The question is about loss of pleasure or interest in activities nearly every day, which most directly relates to diminished motivation and social interest.

patient.answer:
Almost all activities… I don’t know if I’d say almost all, exactly, because there are little moments where something is okay, like if something on the television catches my attention for a minute. But the things I used to really go toward, I just don’t have the push for them anymore.

Like choir—I used to like going, and people know me there. And quilting, I have things sitting there that I could work on. Visiting folks too, people expect me sometimes, and I know that. I’ll even think, “I ought to go,” or “I should call,” and then I just sit there at home with the TV on low, not really watching it much, just letting it be on.

It’s most days like that, I think. Not that I’m crying all day or anything, but the pleasure or the wanting to do it just isn’t there the way it used to be. It feels like I have to push myself for things that used to come natural.

But looking back, that’s about when I started noticing I wasn’t reaching for things the same way. It’s kind of gradually crept up since then, more than something that happened in one week or one month.
